centering_visual_guide.description: What centering deviation percentages LOOK like visually

examples.0-2%: Borders appear nearly identical. You have to look VERY closely to see any difference. This is PRISTINE territory.
examples.2-4%: One border is slightly wider, but you need to examine carefully. Still excellent - GEM MINT eligible.
examples.4-6%: Noticeable difference when comparing borders side-by-side. One border is clearly wider. Upper GEM MINT to MINT.
examples.6-10%: Obviously off-center at a glance. One border is significantly wider (maybe 1.5x the other). MINT range.
examples.10-15%: Clearly shifted. One border might be 2x the width of the other. 8.5 NM-MT+ range.
examples.15%+: Severely off-center. The card looks miscut. 8 NM-MT or lower.

centering_visual_guide.measurement_tip: Compare LEFT border to RIGHT border. If left is 10 units and right is 12 units, deviation = |10-12|/(10+12) = 9.1%

10_PRISTINE.defect_rules: ONLY surface defects allowed (print lines, minor ink). ZERO corner wear. ZERO edge wear.
10_PRISTINE.visual_cue: Card looks absolutely flawless at first glance. Centering is dead-on.

10_GEM_MINT.defect_rules: Max 1 corner touch, 1 edge touch, 2 surface marks. Very minor only.
10_GEM_MINT.rarity: Top 15% of submissions. Still very strict.
10_GEM_MINT.visual_cue: Beautiful card. Maybe one border slightly wider if you look closely.

9_MINT.defect_rules: Small corner dings, light edge wear, surface scratches acceptable.
9_MINT.visual_cue: Nice card with minor imperfections visible on close inspection.

8.5_NM_MT_PLUS.defect_rules: Multiple corner issues, edge whitening, surface wear all acceptable.
8.5_NM_MT_PLUS.rarity: Common grade for played cards in good shape.
8.5_NM_MT_PLUS.visual_cue: Centering noticeably off. Some visible wear on corners/edges.

8_NM_MT.defect_rules: Moderate wear throughout. Multiple defects expected.
8_NM_MT.visual_cue: Obviously off-center or multiple visible defects.

few_shot_examples.reasoning: Near-perfect centering (1.7% front, 3.2% back) both under PRISTINE thresholds. Only surface defects - no structural wear. This is what PRISTINE looks like.

defects.breakdown: 3 surface only (2 front scratches, 1 back print line), 0 corners, 0 edges

few_shot_examples.reasoning: PERFECT front centering (0.0%). Back at 3.7% still under 4% threshold. Only surface defects - zero structural wear qualifies for PRISTINE.
Front centering excellent (2.0%) but BACK centering at 7.0% exceeds PRISTINE threshold of 4%. Despite only 1 defect, back centering drops it to GEM MINT.
Front centering at 12.9% is significantly off (exceeds 10% MINT threshold). 6 defects across all categories. Despite perfect back centering, front issues drop this to 8.5.
Back centering at 13.6% is severely off - this alone caps the grade at 8. Even with only 3 defects, the back centering kills any chance of 9+.

common_mistakes.mistake: Assuming good front centering means good overall centering
common_mistakes.correction: ALWAYS check back centering separately. Back can be much worse than front.

common_mistakes.mistake: Over-grading vintage holos because they 'look nice'
common_mistakes.correction: Vintage cards often have surface/centering issues. Be strict, not nostalgic.

common_mistakes.mistake: Counting holofoil texture as surface defects
common_mistakes.correction: Natural holofoil pattern is NOT a defect. Look for scratches, print lines, ink spots.

common_mistakes.mistake: Being too generous with centering estimates
common_mistakes.correction: When in doubt, the centering is probably WORSE than you think. TAG is strict.

grading_philosophy: TAG uses a 1000-point system that is MORE STRICT than PSA or BGS. When uncertain between two grades, TAG almost always gives the LOWER grade. Your estimates should lean conservative, especially on centering.
